purpose: Five additional illustrative Flight Lab concepts; geometry, telemetry, routes and performance curves are generated artwork, not numerical validation data.

variants.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished 16:9 desktop concept screenshot for TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab 'Mission overview'. Distinct MAP-FIRST engineering layout, light slate app shell, clear turquoise reference route and blue actual route, restrained amber event pins. Exact main header 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', subheading 'Mission overview', top right 'Design concept'. Most screen shows a precise flat top-down terrain map with subtle contour lines, a simple aircraft marker, four clearly numbered route waypoints, cyan dashed reference and solid blue actual track, one amber pin 'Wingtip loss · 20 s'. No satellite-provider brand. Left compact route list 'Waypoint 1', 'Waypoint 2', 'Waypoint 3', 'Waypoint 4', 'Selected route', buttons 'Import route' 'Export config'. Right stacked panel includes a modest 3D inset of a plausible schematic F-16 above coordinate grid, title 'Aircraft view', a simple altitude profile line chart 'Altitude profile', a short event list. Bottom shared timeline with a blue scrubber and amber event tick, 't = 24.6 s', button 'Open replay'. Include small 'Illustrative route · Guidance layer required'. No invented performance score, no battle icons, no huge instrument clutter, no device mockup. Prioritize readable English labels and cartographic clarity. Concept demonstrates overview of spatial route and events, distinct from telemetry-heavy analysis and 3D component editing.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one 16:9 desktop concept screenshot for TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab 'Fault investigation'. Neutral warm-white engineering case-review interface with slate text, cobalt tracking lines and amber failure highlights. Header 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', main title 'Fault investigation', selected event pill 'Wingtip loss · 20.0 s', badge 'Design concept'. Main upper area three aligned cards showing a schematic F-16 in the same camera orientation at three stages, titles 'Before event' 'Event boundary' 'Recovery'; middle left wingtip amber, third aircraft banked gently. A clean central timeline aligns snapshots and orange event boundary at 20 s. Lower left two aligned plots 'Applied actuator input' and 'Roll response', readable axes and short legends, shared amber vertical event cursor. Right sidebar 'Recorded evidence' with sections 'Event applied', 'Affected component: Left tip', 'Commanded vs applied input', 'State estimates', and deliberate status 'Causal interpretation requires review'. Small expandable rows 'Model metadata' 'Controller metadata'. Footer controls 'Previous event' 'Next event' 'Export evidence'. Tiny 'Illustrative data'. This UI lets a researcher inspect recorded evidence; do not claim root cause automatically or show definitive result badges. Legible sparse short English labels, consistent units, no device frame, no holograms, no military badges.

Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a high fidelity 16:9 concept screenshot of a TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab compact Jupyter notebook widget. Light academic notebook canvas with familiar understated notebook cells, no third party logos. Header 'Flight Lab · Notebook view', badge 'Design concept'. Upper page brief markdown-style heading 'F-16 fault recovery experiment', one short plain configuration summary 'Controller AA-INDI · Seed 47 · Wingtip loss at 20 s', avoid long source code. The principal notebook output is a neatly bordered embedded widget, horizontally split into left 3D pane showing schematic F-16 with amber wingtip on white coordinate grid, right two aligned scientific plots 'Roll tracking' and 'Actuator input', actual blue and reference dashed gray, amber fault line at 20 s. Below widget a compact shared replay slider and 't = 24.6 s', small controls 'Play', '1×', 'Expand', 'Export HTML'. Below output next notebook block 'Experiment notes' with readable one sentence 'Inspect the applied inputs around the failure boundary.' Sidebar optional very narrow table of contents 'Setup' 'Replay' 'Notes'. Footer 'Illustrative data · Portable replay'. Design emphasizes a compact usable embedded visual without changing the notebook workflow; readable sparse English labels, clear plot axis units, no dense unreadable code, no full giant telemetry dashboard, no fabricated benchmark claims, no device mockup, no excessive shadows. Crisp editorial notebook screenshot with generous whitespace and engineering clarity.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished 16:9 flat desktop design concept for TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab 'Learning workspace'. Sophisticated dark charcoal research dashboard, teal and purple accent data series, amber fault events. Top 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', selected tab 'Learning', badge 'Design concept'. Left small experiment list 'PPO', 'SAC', 'IHDP', selected run 'IHDP · Seed 47'. Upper main content two wide learning charts 'Evaluation tracking error' and 'Control effort', line curves with subtle shaded uncertainty bands, neutral unlabeled numeric y ticks and x axis 'Evaluation step', avoid claiming a performance win. Upper-right metadata cards 'Training status Paused', 'Checkpoint 12', 'Evaluation seeds 5', no numeric success claims. Lower main portion has a compact 3D replay of a gray schematic F-16 with trajectory above coordinate grid title 'Selected evaluation replay', alongside chart 'Roll tracking' with shared time cursor and one orange 'Fault event' marker. Narrow right panel 'Recorded diagnostics' rows 'Model prediction error', 'Applied actuator input', 'Policy updates', 'Constraint violations', with modest sparklines and 'Inspect run' button. Bottom controls 'Select checkpoint', 'Open replay', 'Export metrics', footer 'Illustrative metrics · Evaluation separate from training'. Show purposeful hierarchy between training/evaluation histories and one replay; charts and checkpoint metadata are illustrative, no rewards leaderboard, no trophies, no fabricated state-of-the-art claim, no neon holograms, no cluttered source code, no device mockup. Readable short English labels. Concept for observing adaptation and selecting evaluation artifacts.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one 16:9 high-fidelity app concept screenshot for TensorAeroSpace Flight Lab 'Presentation mode'. Cinematic but restrained scientific replay viewer, full-width 3D scene with a plausible unarmed gray F-16 in gentle bank above understated mountains in daylight, cyan reference path and blue actual trajectory ribbons. Minimal dark translucent application chrome: top left 'TensorAeroSpace / Flight Lab', title 'Recorded flight replay', top right badge 'Design concept'. Scene fills 80 percent of image; a small amber callout 'Wingtip loss · 20.0 s' identifies a tip region with no explosions. Left compact overlay 'AA-INDI', 'F-16 nonlinear', 'Seed 47'; bottom-right discreet telemetry strip 'Airspeed 200 m/s', 'Altitude 2500 m', 'Roll 12°', 't = 24.6 s'. Lower overlay a narrow synchronized strip chart 'Roll tracking' with actual blue and dashed reference, single amber fault tick, clean minimal replay scrubber. Bottom controls 'Chase camera' 'Orbit' 'Hide overlays' 'Export frame' 'Exit presentation'. Persistent visible 'Illustrative replay · Concept artwork'. Strong visual storytelling and readability for lectures and demos, terrain is a visual backdrop, not a validated digital twin; no performance winners, military insignia, weapon details, combat scenes, holograms, giant cockpit instruments, or device frame. Attractive but believable engineering replay presentation with enough scientific context to identify the experiment.
